build: v130 Private Repo Day One Script
purpose: Turn the backend alpha control board into a practical private repository day-one script for preflight, repo creation, branch setup, starter shell, taxonomy, issues, first PR, workflow check names, branch protection, and closeout proof.
scriptKpis: How ready the private repo day is to run from one command script.
Preflight, repo, branch, files, taxonomy, issues, PR, checks, protection, closeout.
Screenshots and evidence notes that must be captured by a person.
Any secret, public repo, workbook, or commercial leak stops the day immediately.
preflightChecklist: Confirm GitHub login, expected account, local folder, Node version, and package manager.
No customer workbook, secret, certificate, invoice, payment key, or production data may enter the repo.
Controlled repo opening is approved; live SaaS, live billing, and live customer data stay out of scope.
Prepare local evidence path before running commands so proof does not get lost.
Use `dhirajnyse/pursuitdesk-platform` unless the owner deliberately renames the production backend repo.
The first PR can be closed without merge; no database, billing, or customer action is irreversible.
commandBlocks: gh auth status; git --version; node --version; npm --version
Confirms local operator identity and basic tooling before any repo action.
Creates the private production backend repository; capture visibility proof immediately.
git clone git@github.com:dhirajnyse/pursuitdesk-platform.git; cd pursuitdesk-platform; git checkout -b codex/backend-alpha-shell
Keeps main clean and starts all work on a reviewable branch.
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force apps/api/src packages/domain packages/db infra docs/evidence .github/workflows scripts
Creates the minimum repo skeleton for backend alpha work.
Copy only approved root, API, package, workflow, env-example, script, and evidence files from the v129/v130 packs.
Moves generated shell files only; no Excel source files, secrets, or live credentials.
npm install; npm run lint; npm run test -- --runInBand
Runs available proof commands or records exact placeholders linked to issues if scripts are not ready.
Create 35 labels and 7 milestones from the taxonomy pack, then capture the labels and milestones screens.
Makes issue routing visible before backlog import.
Open the first M0/M1 wave from 12 generated issue bodies and record each URL in evidence.
Creates traceability before the first PR is opened.
git add .; git commit -m "Backend alpha shell"; git push -u origin codex/backend-alpha-shell; gh pr create --draft --title "Backend alpha shell" --body-file docs/evidence/first-pr.md
Creates a draft first PR with proof, rollback, risk reference, and reviewer lanes.
Capture 8 workflow check names after the first Actions run, then apply branch protection only with real check names.
Ends with branch protection proof, owner signoffs, blockers, and next owner.
manualActions: Capture private visibility before files or issues move.
Write that no source workbook, .env, certificate, customer file, or commercial export entered the repo.
Save the starter tree showing apps, packages, infra, docs, workflows, scripts, and evidence.
Paste the first wave URLs into `docs/evidence/issue-wave.md`.
Add scope, commands, rollback, open blockers, risk reference, and reviewer lanes to the PR body.
Copy exact GitHub check names before creating branch protection rules.
Capture required checks, PR review rules, conversation resolution, and bypass decision.
Record passed, deferred, blocked, next owner, and go/hold/no-go status.
evidenceFiles: Tool versions, GitHub identity, local path, decision owner, and no-live-data boundary.
Private visibility proof, repo URL, owner, and timestamp.
No secrets, no workbooks, no certificates, no invoices, no commercial leak.
Folder tree and approved starter files copied.
Issue URLs, labels, milestones, owners, and opening order.
PR title, link, scope, commands, rollback, reviewers, risk note, and blockers.
Exact workflow names, job names, required checks, and artifact links.
Main protection rules, required checks, review settings, and bypass note.
Passed, deferred, blocked, owners, next action, and decision log.
issueWaveScript: Open root docs, workspace, scripts, env examples, and evidence folder issues first.
Open tenant guard, commercial redaction, no-secret scan, and denied-audit issues.
Open health, auth, users, records, commercial vault, import, billing, feedback, and audit routes.
Open migration order, fixture seed, source trace, duplicate quarantine, and rollback issues.
Open workflow, release-gate, artifact, check-name, and branch-protection issues.
Open USD plans, test checkout, seat reconciliation, access locks, and billing audit issues.
prScript: Keep the PR narrow and clearly non-production.
Root docs, package shells, API route shells, workflows, env examples, scripts, evidence notes.
No production deployment, no customer workbook, no live payment key, no real billing capture.
Preflight, install, lint/test placeholders, issue URLs, clean-copy scan, and file tree.
No migration or customer data is applied; branch can be deleted and repo can be recreated if needed.
Founder/product, platform, backend, security, data, and QA/release.
branchProtectionTiming: GitHub check names do not exist yet, so guessing creates broken protection.
Copy workflow, job, and check labels exactly as GitHub displays them.
Make sure review policy matches product, platform, backend, security, data, and QA ownership.
Require PR, required checks, review approval, and conversation resolution.
Confirm the protection blocks unsafe merge and produces expected status names.
Write branch protection evidence and unresolved exceptions into closeout notes.
stopScript: Stop before adding files, switch to private or recreate, then document the event.
Stop, remove, rotate, check history, and write an incident note.
Stop and restart from generated fixtures only.
Remove value, LOA, agreement, invoice, billing, and negotiation data from operational examples.
Pause until the owner confirms go/hold/no-go.
Do not apply branch protection until exact check names appear.
Add issue link, scope, proof, rollback, blockers, and reviewer lanes before review.
Write proof files before closing the day.
ownerPrompts: Do you approve repo opening only, with no live data and no production launch?
Can you prove private visibility, branch discipline, workflow names, and main protection?
Can you own starter files, scripts, route shells, and first PR quality proof?
Can you confirm no secrets, no live data, tenant guard scope, and commercial redaction?
Can you confirm generated fixtures only, migration rollback, and no workbook import?
Can you confirm evidence files, screenshots, branch rules, blockers, and closeout?
closeoutChecks: Private repository URL and visibility proof are saved.
Working branch and first PR link are saved.
First issue URLs, labels, milestones, and owner lanes are written.
Tooling, install, quality, placeholder, and release-gate output are captured.
No secrets, no workbooks, no customer files, and no commercial fields are present.
Exact check names and any failed check reasons are recorded.
Branch protection proof exists or a dated defer reason is written.
The next implementation owner and first backlog move are explicit.
handoff: v130 turns the control board into a practical private repo day-one script.
The script is deliberately staged: prove identity, private repo, clean copy set, folder shell, issues, first PR, workflow names, branch protection, and closeout.
It stays honest about what cannot be automated in this static demo: real GitHub repo creation, real Actions check names, real reviewer assignment, and real owner signoff.
v131 can convert this script into a proof exporter that generates the evidence folder, note templates, PR body, and closeout files for the private repo.
